goal: Say ba pa ma fa in all four tones, hear b from p, and learn your first 4 words.

items.note: No puff of air on the b.
A strong puff of air on the p, then a sharp fall.
The second ma is short and light: the neutral tone.
Falling, then a short, light ba.

steps.title: The Pinyin chart
steps.text:
Every Chinese syllable is built the same way: an **initial** (the consonant at the start), a **final** (the rest) and a **tone** (the pitch).

The Pinyin chart lists all of them, about 400. Each lesson teaches one block of it.

Today's block: **b p m f** with the final **a**. That **a** is the open *a* of German *Vater* or English *father*. On its own it's a syllable too: **a**.

steps.title: b and p: the puff of air
steps.text:
Hold your hand in front of your mouth.

**p** comes with a strong puff of air, like English *pie* or a firm German *P*.

**b** has no puff. It isn't a buzzing English *b* either: think of the *p* in English *spy*, or a soft southern German *b*.

**m** and **f** are the same as in English and German.

steps.title: Every syllable has a tone
steps.text:
A tone is a pitch shape. Change the tone and you get a different word. Here is **ma** in the four tones. Just listen.

You'll always practise all four together: hearing them side by side is how you learn to tell them apart.

steps.title: 1st tone: high and flat
steps.text:
Start high and hold it, like singing one note.

English: the *Aaah* at the doctor's. German: a sung *Laaa*.

The mark is a flat line: **ā**. As a number: **a1**. The top row has all four tones to compare.

steps.title: 2nd tone: rising
steps.text:
Start in the middle and go up, like a surprised *What?* German: *Was?*, or *Ja?* answering the phone.

The mark rises from left to right: **á**. As a number: **a2**.

steps.title: 3rd tone: low
steps.text:
Drop your voice low and keep it relaxed. A bit creaky is fine.

English: a low, doubtful *Hmm…* German: a reluctant *Na ja…*

Said on its own it often rises a little at the end. Inside a sentence it mostly just stays **low**, so think *low*, not *down-up*.

The mark is a little valley: **ǎ**. As a number: **a3**.

steps.title: 4th tone: a sharp fall
steps.text:
Start high and drop fast, like a firm *No!* German: *Nein!* or *Doch!*

The mark falls from left to right: **à**. As a number: **a4**.

steps.title: Your first block of the chart
steps.text: Tap a square to hear it. Tap a syllable on the left to hear it in all four tones, or a tone at the top to hear the whole column. Draw the shapes in the air with your hand: high, rising, low, falling.

steps.title: The neutral tone
steps.text:
Some syllables have no tone of their own. They're said short and light, straight after the syllable before. This is the **neutral tone**. It has no mark; as a number it's **5** (or no number at all).

Your next two words end in one: **māma** and **bàba**.
